sources.title: Qur'an, Surah al-Asr (103:1-3)
sources.inspected_scope: All three displayed Arabic verses, 103:1-3; HTML extraction includes word-by-word and complete-verse text. Displayed English translation inspected for orientation but not reproduced as the chapter translation.
supports: Arabic wording and order
Three-verse composition
Repeated wa-tawasaw bi- expression
Verse-end lexical forms
sources.usage_notes: Chapter uses ordinary vowelled Arabic spelling, not a claimed exact reproduction of Uthmani glyphs or recitation signs. English translation is original and provisional.
gaps: This display alone does not document every reading tradition or establish a historical text-critical argument

sources.title: The Quranic Arabic Corpus: Word by Word, Chapter 103
sources.author: Kais Dukes and Quranic Arabic Corpus contributors
sources.inspected_scope: Word-by-word annotations for 103:1:1 through 103:3:9, all displayed on the opened page.
supports: Opening wa is an oath particle
La in lafi is emphatic
Illa is an exceptive particle
Plural relative and verbal forms
Tawasaw annotated as form VI perfect third-person masculine plural
sources.usage_notes: A useful independently inspectable annotation, not an infallible grammatical authority or a literary-excellence measurement. Inna emphasis also checked in al-Razi; the corpus labels it an accusative particle.
gaps: Form VI does not warrant a blanket claim that every verb of that form has the same reciprocal meaning

sources.title: Jami al-bayan an tawil ay al-Quran, commentary on Surah al-Asr
sources.author: Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari
sources.inspected_scope: Complete short commentary displayed for 103:1 and 103:3. The 103:3 page initially timed out and then loaded successfully on retry.
sources.verified_locator: Commentary on 103:1, concluding judgment beginning والصواب من القول; commentary on 103:3, explanation of collective al-insan and both tawasaw clauses
supports: Reported temporal interpretations of asr and al-Tabari's inclusive conclusion
Al-insan explained collectively to account for plural exception
Tawasi explained as some counseling others
Truth linked to revelation and patience to obedience
sources.usage_notes: Reports establish what al-Tabari transmits, not independent authentication of each report. Displayed page 601 refers to Quran navigation and is not cited as a commentary page.
gaps: Printed edition and page collation pending
Comparative manuscript or variant-reading analysis outside inspected scope

sources.title: Al-Kashshaf, commentary on Surah al-Asr
sources.author: Abu al-Qasim Mahmud ibn Umar al-Zamakhshari
sources.inspected_scope: Commentary on 103:1 including alternate oath referents; commentary on 103:3 explaining truth and patience. Unrelated site catalogue was not treated as textual evidence.
sources.verified_locator: 103:1 paragraph beginning أقسم بصلاة العصر; 103:3 paragraph beginning والمعنى أن الناس في خسران
supports: Prayer, afternoon, and time presented as alternate readings
Religiously contextualized interpretation of truth
Patience interpreted with reference to obedience, restraint, and trials
sources.usage_notes: A hadith-like reward report appears at the end of 103:3. It is deliberately not used because its authenticity was not investigated. The website's general edition description does not establish the edition of this particular transcription.
gaps: Printed edition and page collation pending
Do not infer that all alternate meanings must be simultaneously intended

sources.title: Mafatih al-ghayb, commentary on Qur'an 103:2
sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (work attributed under this name by the digital source)
sources.inspected_scope: 103:2 issues one through four and the paragraph listing emphasis by inna, lam, and fi khusr. Opening issues on 103:3 also inspected, but not used as a substantive chapter authority because of an apparent transcription problem in the displayed passage.
sources.verified_locator: 103:2 المسألة الأولى; concluding discussion beginning واعلم أن الله تعالى قرن بهذه الآية قرائن
supports: Generic and particular-person interpretations of al-insan are recorded
Inna and lam identified as emphatic
Fi khusr interpreted as immersion or encompassing loss
sources.usage_notes: Cited observations rely on 103:2. The 103:3 transcription contains a phrase involving الذين كفروا in an argument about coordinated faith and action that requires print checking before quotation or analysis. No claim about authorship of disputed portions of the commentary is resolved here.
gaps: Printed edition and page collation pending
Historical reports about named opponents not authenticated
Authorship/completion history of the full work not independently investigated

sources.title: Al-Tahrir wa-l-tanwir, commentary on Qur'an 103:2-3
sources.author: Muhammad al-Tahir Ibn Ashur
sources.inspected_scope: Complete displayed commentary on 103:2; displayed commentary on 103:3 including special-after-general analysis and mutual counsel.
sources.verified_locator: 103:2 paragraphs beginning وتعريف الإنسان and والظرفية; 103:3 paragraph beginning وعطف على عمل الصالحات
supports: Generic expression qualified with reference to historical addressees
Spatial fi interpreted as figurative enclosure
Loss interpreted in relation to ultimate outcome
Mutual counsel singled out after righteous action as a particular within a general category
sources.usage_notes: Chapter paraphrases selectively rather than reproducing the commentary. Conclusions reflect Ibn Ashur's interpretation, not unanimous grammatical necessity. Site catalogue mentions a Tunis 1984 publication but the chapter does not claim that edition was inspected.
